rule.description: One coherent rule family: production code that can never execute. A statement is dead when an unconditional terminator statically precedes it; a guarded region is dead when its guard reads a module-level configuration literal whose fixed value makes the region unreachable (a disabled feature switch, an always-on flag with a terminated accepting branch, or a never-entered loop); a production symbol (module function, class, method, module constant, or import binding) is dead when no reachable production code path references it - references that exist only inside statically dead regions or only inside other unreferenced symbols keep the symbol dead.

checks.description: Pylint stock 'unreachable' check (W0101) enabled as part of this case's rule family: statements statically unreachable because an unconditional return/raise/break/continue precedes them in the same block.
checks.why_this_is_the_smell: The statement executes as part of the function body's syntactic flow but no runtime path can reach it, so the code is dead while still claiming a place in the production file.

matches.evidence: The announcement call after 'return incrementer, blockchain' is unreachable: W0101 at miner.py:126, 'Unreachable code (unreachable)'.

checks.description: A guard reads a module-level configuration constant whose fixed literal value makes one side of the branch permanently unreachable: a False flag disables the guarded region, a True flag with a terminated accepting branch disables everything after it, and a False while-condition never enters the loop.
checks.detected_relation: module-level configuration switch -> permanently disabled production code path
checks.why_this_is_the_smell: The branch is wired into a live production flow, yet the committed configuration makes it impossible to ever execute, so the region plus everything it exists for is dead code the maintainers still maintain.

matches.evidence: W9001 at miner.py:229: guard 'LEGACY_COMMAND_PROTOCOL_ENABLED' is statically always-False (module constant fixed to False), so the retired command-protocol chain fetch guarded by it can never run.
W9001 at miner.py:253: guard 'STRICT_CHAIN_VALIDATION' is statically always-True with a terminated accepting branch ('return True'), so the relaxed-mode fallback that follows can never execute.
W9001 at wallet.py:90: guard 'WALLET_EXPLORER_ENABLED' is statically always-False (module constant fixed to False), so the explorer-chain preview printed on the receipt side can never run.

checks.description: A production symbol (module function, class, method, module constant, or import binding) has no reference from any reachable production code path: reference counting runs a cross-module liveness fixpoint in which only reachable statements count, so references made solely inside statically dead regions or inside other unreferenced symbols leave the symbol dead.
checks.detected_relation: production symbol -> live production code path
checks.why_this_is_the_smell: The symbol augments the production module's public surface and must be read, reviewed, and kept consistent, yet nothing that can execute ever reaches it.

matches.evidence: W9002 at miner.py:129: its only reference sits inside the unreachable tail of proof_of_work (see check pylint-unreachable-statement), so all 1 reference(s) sit inside statically dead code.
W9002 at miner.py:208: its only reference is the call guarded by the always-False LEGACY_COMMAND_PROTOCOL_ENABLED switch in consensus, so all 1 reference(s) sit inside statically dead code.

excluded.reason: Construction machinery of a live class: Block(0, ...) in create_genesis_block executes at import, so the constructor path is reachable and dunder methods are entry points rather than dead symbols.
Flask route handlers stay live through decorator registration with the node app, which is a deployment entry point even though no in-module call site exists.

The startup guard's test is a runtime-environment comparison, not a fixed module constant, and the startup block is the canonical process entry point; the rule resolves guards only against committed configuration literals.

excluded.symbol: while True mining loop in mine
excluded.reason: An always-true loop is a deliberate continuous computation whose body executes; the rule flags never-entered loops (constant-False condition), not intentional infinite loops.
The bare except wraps a reachable verification call; reachable-but-poorly-scoped error handling is a different smell from dead code.

The checker analyzes the three production modules (miner.py, wallet.py, miner_config.py) with Pylint; test code is an oracle for behavior, not production surface, and reference counting is production-only by design.

excluded.symbol: LEGACY_COMMAND_PROTOCOL_ENABLED / STRICT_CHAIN_VALIDATION / WALLET_EXPLORER_ENABLED in the injected state
excluded.reason: In the injected state these three flags are read by the guard statements themselves from reachable lines, so the reference rule keeps them live; a repair that deletes the guards without deleting the flags correctly turns them into new checker matches. Negative-reference restraint clarifies the ownership boundary: deadness is measured at repair time, never assumed.

excluded.symbol: module docstring and inline comment text
excluded.reason: Commented prose and historical notes are documentation; the rule reports statically dead executable statements, not discussion of retired behaviour.
